# Full-Screen Zoom on the Match Screen

> Operator request, 2026-08-06: *"on the match video screen when looking at the selected video, the image on the screen needs a click to expand feature and the expanded image should support pinch to zoom."*
## What was wrong
The match screen is where the operator decides whether their video and a candidate are the **same work**. That decision is frequently made on a detail — a logo, a room, a face in the background — and neither side of the comparison could be enlarged:
- The candidate's images opened into a grid, and the grid cells were static. No zoom anywhere.
- The **selected video's own preview frames** were explicitly non-interactive. `DetailGridView` carried the comment *"a tap would have nowhere to go"*, which was true when written — there is no player behind that screen to seek.
So the screen asked for a judgement it would not let you look closely enough to make.
## What was built
⚠️ **Nothing about pinch-to-zoom was written from scratch.** A full-screen zoomable browser already existed as two private nested types inside `ProfileGraphHeaderView`, and it carries two hard-won fixes a re-write would not have known to reproduce:
- the pager's centring (an extra offset once made tapping a thumbnail open the **next** photo)
- the deliberate gap between the edge tap zones, so a double-tap aimed at resetting zoom does not turn two pages
Both were extracted to `ZoomablePhotoBrowser.swift` as `ZoomablePhoto` and `WrappingPhotoPager`, generic over their content. `ProfileGraphHeaderView` now uses the shared pair, so there is **one** implementation rather than two to keep in step.
Built on them:
| Screen | Browser | Opens on |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Candidate images grid | `RemotePhotoBrowser` | the image tapped, not the first |
| The video's own preview frames | `VideoFrameBrowser` | the frame tapped |
Both support pinch to zoom (to 5×), double-tap to reset, swipe and edge-tap to page, and wrap endlessly.
## Details worth keeping
- **The frame browser reuses ****`FrameExtractView`**, so a frame already decoded for the grid is served from the same cache rather than decoded again at size.
- **Its title is the timestamp, not "3 of 16".** On a video the useful thing about a frame is where in the running time it came from.
- **Zoom state is per page** (`.id` on each). The pager renders exactly three fixed slots, so without this a page change carries a stale scale onto a different picture.
- **Tap-to-expand on frames is gated on ****`isInteractive == false`****.** Where there IS a player, a tap still belongs to it — seeking is the more useful action and this must not steal it.
- The grid cells carry a small expand affordance, because nothing else distinguishes an interactive grid from a static contact sheet.
## Verification
macOS and iOS build; LibraryCore 1,041 tests, 0 failures; D9 clean. ⚠️ Not device-verified — gesture behaviour, and the interaction between pinch and the pager's drag in particular, is exactly the kind of thing that only a device confirms.
## Related defect — Delete Video was unreachable, not missing
Operator, 2026-08-06: *"The ability to delete a video needs to be returned to the UI in the ellipsis button. It has disappeared from the page."*
🚨 **It had not been removed.** Commit `6d2855d` (31 Jul, the operator's own) had already moved `Delete Video` out of a `DisclosureGroup(\"Danger Zone\")` and into the ⋯ menu, exactly as requested. `git log -S` on both strings shows the removal and the addition in the same commit.
The real defect, visible only from a screenshot of the device: **the menu was taller than the screen.** At the operator's text size every row wraps to two or three lines, and seven rows ran past the bottom of the display — taking `Delete Video…` with them, because a destructive action belongs last. Present, rendered, and unreachable, which reads exactly like having been removed.
⚠️ **The lesson is about verification, not about the menu.** Reading the source proved the action existed and pointed at the wrong conclusion twice — first that the operator must be on the batch inspector, then that the toolbar must be hidden. Neither was true. Only the screenshot showed the actual failure, and no amount of further reading would have found it: the bug is in the interaction between a fixed menu and a variable text size, which is not visible in the code at all.
**Fixed** by making the menu fit rather than hoping it scrolls:
- `Edit Video (Trim / Flip)` → `Trim / Flip`n- The two regenerate actions folded into one `Regenerate` submenu — two multi-line rows become one, and they are a genuine pair.n- Seven top-level rows down to five plus the divider and delete.
Also corrected: the in-app help still told people delete lived "In the Danger Zone section", three weeks after that section was deleted. It now names the ⋯ menu and the macOS `⌘⌫` shortcut.
⚠️ Sizing at accessibility text sizes is not something a build verifies. This needs the operator to open the menu on the phone and confirm `Delete Video…` is now visible without scrolling.
